holidays.name: National Goof Off Day
holidays.description: A day to put down the spreadsheets, ditch the to-do list and do something delightfully pointless. Think blanket forts, paper airplane contests or a midday nap. Productivity can wait until tomorrow.
holidays.origin: Chase's Calendar of Events editor William D. Chase created it in 1976. His granddaughter, Monica Dufour, helped inspire the idea. It was meant to give hard-working people a guilt-free excuse to slack off.
holidays.funFact: Chase's Calendar of Events is one of the world's best-known references for quirky observances. The creator of National Goof Off Day was himself in the business of cataloguing offbeat holidays.

holidays.name: National Bavarian Crepes Day
holidays.description: A salute to wafer-thin, pancake-like treats that are rolled up around fruit, cream, chocolate or jam. You can fill them with sweet things, dust them with sugar, or drizzle on a glaze.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance held every March 22. The treat is rooted in Central and Eastern European kitchens, where thin pancakes are a classic dessert.
holidays.funFact: Bavarian crepes are not true French crêpes. The batter is cooked right away rather than left to rest, and the dish is closely related to the palatschinke.

holidays.name: World Water Day
holidays.description: A global day to celebrate fresh water and bring attention to the billions of people who still lack safe drinking water. It's a good excuse to appreciate your tap and to think about how to conserve water.
holidays.origin: The United Nations General Assembly designated March 22 as World Water Day after the 1992 UN Conference on Environment and Development. It has been observed annually since 1993.
holidays.funFact: Each year's observance has a different theme. Past themes have covered topics such as wastewater, groundwater and water scarcity.
